What is CSS specificity?

what does numpy do
NumPy provides dense n-dimensional arrays with vectorised operations implemented in C. Boxz uses it for every matrix multiplication, activation and gradient computation in the model.
what is backpropagation

Backpropagation is the chain rule applied to a computation graph in reverse order. Each operation knows its local derivative; the engine multiplies incoming gradients by those derivatives and accumulates them per parameter.
what is gradient descent
Gradient descent updates parameters in the direction that reduces loss: p = p - lr * grad. Boxz uses AdamW, which rescales the update by running estimates of the gradient mean and variance.
what is overfitting

Overfitting is when a model memorises training data instead of learning regularities, so validation loss rises while training loss falls. Dropout, weight decay, more data and early stopping all help. Boxz watches validation loss and keeps the best checkpoint.
what is a learning rate schedule

A learning rate schedule changes the step size during training. Boxz warms up linearly so early updates are gentle, then decays with a cosine curve so the final steps fine tune instead of oscillating.
explain attention

Attention mixes information between positions. Each position projects to a query, a key and a value; scores are query-key dot products scaled by the square root of the head dimension, masked so a position cannot see the future, softmaxed into weights, and used to average the values.

what is a tokenizer?
A tokenizer maps text to integers. Boxz converts bytes to unicode-ish symbols, then merges the most frequent pairs until it reaches 2048 vocabulary entries.
what is attention?
Attention lets each position look at earlier positions and mix their information. Queries meet keys to produce weights, and those weights average the values.
why is attention causal?
Because a language model must not see the future. Each position may only attend to itself and earlier positions, which is enforced with a triangular mask.
what is a parameter?
A number the training loop adjusts. Boxz has about five million of them: weight matrices, biases and normalisation scales.
what is a gradient?
The derivative of the loss with respect to a parameter. Training moves each parameter a small step opposite its gradient.
what is backpropagation?
The chain rule applied backwards through the computation graph. Each operation multiplies the incoming gradient by its local derivative.
what is an epoch?
One pass over the training data. Boxz usually samples random windows instead, so progress is counted in steps and tokens.
what is overfitting?
When training loss keeps falling while held-out loss rises: the model memorises examples instead of learning patterns.
what is a learning rate?
The size of an optimiser step. Too high and the loss oscillates; too low and training crawls.
what is loss?
A number measuring how wrong the prediction was. Boxz uses cross entropy, the negative log probability assigned to the correct token.
what is perplexity?
The exponential of the mean cross-entropy loss. Lower is better; it roughly means how many tokens the model is choosing between.
what is a checkpoint?
A saved copy of the weights, the tokenizer and the training state, so a run can be resumed or served later.
what is the difference between training and inference?
Training adjusts weights with gradients. Inference only runs the forward pass, usually without building a graph.
what does temperature do?
It divides the logits before the softmax. Low temperature makes the choice sharper, high temperature more random.
what does top-k sampling do?
It keeps only the k most likely tokens, renormalises, and samples from those. It removes the long tail of unlikely words.
what is top-p sampling?
Also called nucleus sampling: keep the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum to p, then sample inside that set.
what is a kv cache?
During generation the keys and values of earlier tokens do not change, so they are cached instead of recomputed every step.
